reasoning_steps: The claim that "lightning never strikes the same place twice" is a common myth that is factually false

According to the National Weather Service (NWS), lightning frequently strikes the same place repeatedly, particularly tall, pointed, isolated structures that provide an optimal conductive path between the ground and charged storm clouds
For instance, the NWS notes that the Empire State Building in New York City is struck by lightning an average of 23 to 25 times per year.
